title: Real-account concurrency smoke: 500 messages processed concurrently up to the 250 cap
asA: developer verifying the facade works against a real Cloudflare account
iWant: a smoke test that publishes 500 messages against the shared CI queue rcf-lite-ci-queue-smoke and asserts the consumer processes them concurrently up to the documented 250-invocation cap
soThat: the shipped shape's compatibility with the real Cloudflare Queues surface is proven end-to-end at least once per release, without requiring every CI run to be account-bound

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT=1 and the credentials for the shared CI queue rcf-lite-ci-queue-smoke wired via security-secrets-management, when the real-account-concurrency-smoke probe runs against the real queue, then 500 messages are published, the consumer processes them concurrently up to the 250 push-based invocation cap Cloudflare documents at https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/platform/limits/, and the smoke drains the queue on exit. Without CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT the probe records accountBoundSkipped true per spec section 3.5 and the per-blueprint report carries aggregateVerdict pass.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the shared CI queue rcf-lite-ci-queue-smoke on the maintainer's account, or the env var unset
acceptanceCriteria.then: with the env var set, 500 messages round-trip with observed concurrency below or equal to 250; with the env var unset, the report carries accountBoundSkipped true and aggregateVerdict pass; the shim exits 0 in both paths

acceptanceCriteria.description: Concurrency cap enforced. Given 500 messages published in a burst on the real-account probe, when the consumer processes them, then at no observed moment is the concurrent in-flight count greater than the Cloudflare-documented 250 cap; a mutation SIMULATE_CONCURRENCY_BREACH=true drives the concurrency past 250 and the smoke FAILS naming the observed peak.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the consumer processes them under the real-account probe
acceptanceCriteria.then: in-flight count never exceeds 250; the breach mutation FAILS naming the observed peak
